Legal Requirements

Consent

Data Security

Encryption of data in transit and at rest
Regular security assessments and updates
Access controls and authentication procedures
Secure data storage and backup systems
Employee training on data protection

Data Retention
We retain your personal information only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this Privacy Policy, unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law.
Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update our Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page and updating the "Last Updated" date. You are advised to review this Privacy Policy periodically for any changes.

blocks.text: Facebook Ads Budget Calculator
Tell it how many customers you want each month. It tells you the daily budget to set in Meta Ads Manager.
About 23 leads a week is under the roughly 50 Meta wants per ad set. Run a single ad set and give it two to three weeks before judging the numbers.
Facebook ad budget questions people ask
How much should I spend on Facebook ads?

Work backwards from the customers you want. Customers wanted divided by your close rate gives leads needed. Leads needed times your cost per lead gives the monthly budget. Want 20 customers, close 20% of leads, pay $40 a lead: 100 leads x $40 = $4,000 a month, about $132 a day.
What is a normal cost per lead on Facebook?

It swings a lot by industry and offer. Home services and local businesses often land somewhere around $20 to $80 per lead, while legal, finance, and high-ticket B2B can run well past $100. Use your own numbers if you have them. If you are starting fresh, budget for the high end and let real data bring it down.
Is $10 or $20 a day enough for Facebook ads?

It can get you some results, but it is usually too little to exit the learning phase. Meta wants around 50 conversions per ad set per week to optimize properly. At $40 a lead, that is about $2,000 a week. Small budgets still work, they just learn slower and cost more per result for longer.
Should I set a daily or lifetime budget?

Daily budgets are easier to manage for always-on lead generation because spend stays steady and you can scale 20% at a time. Lifetime budgets suit fixed-date promotions like a sale or event. Meta can spend up to 75% over your daily budget on a given day, but it averages out across the week.
How do I lower my cost per customer?

There are two levers. Lower the cost per lead with a stronger offer and better creative, or raise your close rate by calling leads back fast. Going from a 20% to a 30% close rate cuts your cost per customer by a third without touching the ads.

blocks.text: Customer Lifetime Value Calculator
See what one customer is worth in real profit, how that compares to what you pay to get them, and the most you can afford to spend per customer.
Each customer returns 4.0x what it costs to get them. You have room to spend up to $400 per customer and stay at 3:1.
Lifetime value questions people ask
What is customer lifetime value?

The total a customer is worth to your business over the whole time they buy from you. This calculator shows it two ways: total revenue, and gross profit after your delivery costs. Use the profit number for ad decisions.
How do you calculate LTV?

Average purchase value times purchases per year times years a customer stays, then times your gross margin. A $200 purchase, 4 times a year, for 3 years is $2,400 in revenue. At a 50% margin that customer is worth $1,200 in profit.
What is a good LTV to CAC ratio?

Around 3:1 is the common target. Under 1:1 you lose money on every customer. Between 1:1 and 3:1 you profit on paper but overhead eats most of it. Well above 5:1 usually means you could spend more to grow faster.
What is the most I should pay to get a customer?
Your profit LTV divided by 3. If a customer is worth $1,200 in gross profit, keep your cost per customer under $400. That leaves room for overhead and profit.
How do I estimate customer lifespan?

If you track monthly churn, divide 1 by your churn rate to get months, then divide by 12. At 5% monthly churn, customers stay about 20 months, or 1.7 years. If you do not track it, look at how long your average past customer kept buying.
What is CAC payback period?

How many months of a customer's gross profit it takes to pay back what you spent to get them. Under 12 months is solid for most small businesses. A long payback ties up cash even when the LTV:CAC ratio looks good.

ROAS questions people ask
What is ROAS?
Return on ad spend. Revenue from ads divided by what you spent on those ads. Spend $1,000 and make $4,000 and your ROAS is 4.0.
What is a good ROAS?

Whatever clears your break-even ROAS. A business with 25% margins needs a 4.0 just to break even, while a business with 70% margins is profitable at 1.5. That is why a single "good ROAS" number is misleading.
How do you calculate break-even ROAS?
Divide 1 by your gross profit margin. At a 40% margin, 1 / 0.40 = 2.5. Anything under 2.5 loses money once product and delivery costs come out.
What is the most I can pay to get one customer?
Your average order value times your margin. At a $150 order and 40% margin you can pay up to $60 per purchase before the sale stops making money. Repeat buyers raise that ceiling.
Is ROAS the same as ROI?
No. ROAS only looks at revenue against ad spend. ROI subtracts all your costs, including product, labor, and software. A campaign can show a 3.0 ROAS and still lose money.

Each video shows its price in credits before you generate it. Credits are held when you press Generate and returned automatically if the video fails, is blocked or is canceled before it starts.
